title: Independent auto-body and collision business-contact review
hypothesis: An independently operated auto-body or collision-repair listing with a published business number can enter the existing business-contact workflow. Its number, a collision claim, and a person found in any public business record do not establish current ownership or an owner-confirmed mobile.
ownerSource: No owner-confirming auto-body adapter is implemented. The catalog reports New Jersey MVC auto-body facility licensing, but access and fields are UNKNOWN, so it cannot supply owner evidence in this workflow.
phoneSource: The implemented recipe-A route starts with a published Maps business number. It remains a business-contact candidate until the existing line-type, live, DNC/TCPA, suppression, and duplicate gates pass.

workflow.label: Discover published auto-body business
workflow.detail: Start with the live recipe-A auto-body shop query. A listing and advertised number are business evidence only.

workflow.label: Core collision-repair fit?
workflow.detail: Require auto body, body shop, collision repair, collision center, or collision service evidence. Auto glass, mechanical repair, detailing, dealer, parts, towing, and generic automotive evidence alone do not pass.

workflow.label: Hold adjacent or ambiguous result
workflow.detail: Do not relabel an adjacent automotive service as collision repair without a core auto-body or collision signal.

workflow.label: Independent business check
workflow.detail: Send known automotive chain or franchise matches to review before an owner hypothesis is formed.

workflow.label: Hold brand or multi-location listing
workflow.detail: A branded local outlet can have a published business contact, but its brand pattern does not confirm a local owner or handset.

workflow.label: Published business number present?
workflow.detail: Do not infer a person number from an auto-body listing, collision service claim, or public identity record.

workflow.label: Hold missing business contact
workflow.detail: Keep identity evidence without a published business number out of phone processing.

workflow.label: Business-contact gates
workflow.detail: Require mobile classification, reachability, DNC/TCPA clearance, suppression, duplicate, and freshness checks on the published number. These do not prove ownership of the business or handset.

workflow.label: Hold failed contact gate
workflow.detail: Hold non-mobile, unreachable, DNC/TCPA, suppressed, duplicate, stale, or otherwise unverified contacts.

workflow.label: Independent owner and handset evidence?
workflow.detail: A business name, a collision listing, a mobile line, or a registry role alone is insufficient. Preserve any person only as candidate evidence.

workflow.label: Hold as business contact
workflow.detail: Do not label or deliver an owner-confirmed mobile without separately recorded ownership and handset evidence.

workflow.label: Deliver approved owner-confirmed contact
workflow.detail: Only a workflow recording independent owner evidence and every contact/compliance gate may use this classification.

edges.label: adjacent-only, generic, or no core match

failures.risk: Standalone collision-repair listings are rejected before the brain allow regex because `classifyRelevance` has no `auto_body` profile, while the broad `body|collision|auto` allow regex accepts unrelated automotive results.
failures.mitigation: Add an `auto body` profile with core terms `auto body`, `body shop`, `collision repair`, `collision center`, and `collision service`; make auto glass, mechanical repair, detailing, dealer, parts, towing, and generic automotive adjacent. Replace the brain allow expression with a collision/body-specific pattern after adding the regression cases.

failures.risk: A collision chain, franchise, or multi-location body shop is represented as a locally owner-operated business.
failures.mitigation: Keep the existing automotive chain exclusion ahead of owner classification and hold branded matches for separately supported local-ownership evidence.

failures.risk: A published shop line or a person named by an unavailable registry is represented as an owner-confirmed mobile.
failures.mitigation: Treat published numbers as business-contact candidates and registry people as candidates only; require independent current ownership and handset evidence after every phone/compliance gate.

failures.risk: New Jersey MVC auto-body licensing is used as an implemented source despite catalog access and fields being unknown.
failures.mitigation: Keep the NJ MVC item blocked until an authorized, documented public endpoint establishes its access, permitted use, fields, and owner/contact semantics.

iterations.hypothesis: The implemented discovery gates consistently classify core auto-body and collision listings while excluding adjacent automotive listings and collision chains.
iterations.test: Five-case fixture/code audit on 2026-09-24 using parseDiscoveryCandidate, the live auto_body brain allow regex, and isChain with no external calls or contact data: Precision Auto Body, Independent Collision Center, Metro Auto Glass, Downtown Auto Repair, and Caliber Collision Albany.
iterations.observed: Precision Auto Body classified core with no rejection. Independent Collision Center, Metro Auto Glass, Downtown Auto Repair, and Caliber Collision Albany each had null fit tier and `no_positive_relevance`, although the `body|collision|auto` allow regex accepted all five. isChain marked only Caliber Collision Albany as `caliber collision`; its earlier relevance rejection therefore preempted the chain drop. This tests runtime classification only, not listing coverage, phone line type, owner identity, reachability, DNC, or delivery.
iterations.change: The hypothesis failed for standalone collision listings and exposed an overbroad secondary allow gate. Add the proposed auto-body profile and tighten the allow expression, with these five fixtures retained as a regression test; do not infer an owner or handset from any passing fixture.

iterations.test: Focused synthetic regression checks in tests/lead-engine-industry-corrections.test.ts, lead-engine-reviews.test.ts, lead-engine-gates-jobs.test.ts and lead-engine-jobs.test.ts. No paid provider call.
iterations.observed: A dedicated collision/body-shop profile admits collision-center synonyms and rejects auto-repair/glass/parts-only rows before verification. Historical brain figures and allow field were not changed.
iterations.change: Shared runtime correction integrated. Original source samples are retained with their original denominators; no phone-yield improvement is claimed.

measurement.result: Five synthetic runtime cases: Precision Auto Body core and accepted; Independent Collision Center null/no_positive_relevance; Metro Auto Glass null/no_positive_relevance; Downtown Auto Repair null/no_positive_relevance; Caliber Collision Albany null/no_positive_relevance and chain-tagged `caliber collision`. The live brain allow regex accepted all five. Code audit only, with no live endpoint, phone, identity, or delivery measurement.

cost.note: No clean delivered owner contact was measured. The auto-body brain's historical Anas rates use a different denominator and are not a per-clean cost for this workflow.

implementation.summary: A dedicated collision/body-shop profile admits collision-center synonyms and rejects auto-repair/glass/parts-only rows before verification. Historical brain figures and allow field were not changed. Original review: Auto body is recognized and runs the Maps-first recipe-A route with a published-business-contact and delivery-gate path. The discovery classifier has no auto_body profile, so collision-only results are rejected despite the brain's collision allow term; the same allow regex also admits adjacent automotive text. No owner-confirming auto-body adapter is implemented.

nextMeasurement: After the relevance and allow correction, run the five synthetic cases as regression coverage: core body/collision fixtures must proceed, auto glass and mechanical repair fixtures must be adjacent or rejected, and Caliber Collision must be chain-filtered after relevance. A later authorized outcome study must separately measure trade fit, current owner confirmation, line type, DNC/TCPA, reachability, and delivery.
